[p-1a2b3c] SELinux blocked httpd_t (write) on /srv/app/logs: no label rule for this place
Waiting for your decision, found by basalt on 2026-10-04 10:15 UTC

  SELinux blocked httpd_t from using /srv/app/logs because no rule labels that
  place for it. SELinux denied httpd_t the write permission on /srv/app/logs
  (labeled var_t), 4 times. It is labeled var_t, a type httpd_t may not use;
  httpd_log_t is a type it may use. If you apply it, the assistant will add a
  rule that labels /srv/app/logs and everything below it as httpd_log_t
  (relabeling the files already there).

What will run (exactly these commands, as root, in this order)
  $ semanage fcontext -a -t httpd_log_t '/srv/app/logs(/.*)?'
  $ restorecon -Rv /srv/app/logs

Risk: medium (adds a lasting SELinux rule for /srv/app/logs).
Undo: a snapshot is taken before and after, so you can go back to the state
before the change; a rollback takes effect at the next boot. Note: the labels
of files under /srv are on a separate volume and stay as they are.
  $ sudo basalt snapshots rollback --before p-1a2b3c

Next step
  Apply it:   sudo basalt apply p-1a2b3c
              (without a prompt: sudo basalt apply p-1a2b3c --yes --confirm f381c3f8)
  Ignore it:  sudo basalt ignore p-1a2b3c

Evidence
  - raw: avc:  denied  { write } for comm="nginx" scontext=system_u:system_r:httpd_t:s0
